title: System Control Board, release 2b: the board itself, with start-up and shut-down
why: Decision 0171 §1, §2 and §12 (Jason approved revision 2, 2026-11-18), release 2b of 5; Jason: 'go on 2b'. A new first section in System Configuration, System Control Board, is the control room his example board pictured. The six stages run across the top, the one the system is in lit; maintenance and history say 'coming' (releases 4 and 5). The system's own controls are Run the pre-flight, Start the system, Shut down in order and Pause everything. Below them are the four systems: the Knowledge Engine, Workers, Outside services and the site itself. Each opens to its processes, marked with a green check, red X or grey dash. A process opens under its name to its whole process: its route, its last 24 hours of worker calls from release 2a's ledger (received, stored, updated, to Review, refused, server errors), its crawler task runs and site jobs, its check, and the listings and Review items it touched (each opens in a peek). Its controls are Run its check, Shut it down (tasks first, then the workflow) and Start it. Start it refuses while its check is red: that is the interlock, and it says why. Shut down in order stops the tasks, then the workflows in reverse start-up order, then the master switch and the crawler's Railway schedule. It reads 'stopped, safe' once no crawler run is still going, saying what was kept. Every change goes through Automation, which logs it as before. The board draws itself again every 30 seconds. The Pre-flight page stays as it is, and its lines are also at the foot of the board. Tested: 14 checks on MariaDB (tools/control-board-tests/r2b.php), and rendered at 390px and 1280px with no sideways scroll. No new tables, no migrations. FAQ: one entry.
